title_en: Binhu District People's Procuratorate of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province v. Ma Zhisong et al. — crime of damaging computer information system

full_text_en:
Binhu District People's Procuratorate of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province v. Ma Zhisong et al. — case of disrupting computer information system

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, where a person, in violation of state regulations, deletes, modifies, adds, or interferes with the functions of a computer information system; or deletes, modifies, or adds the data or application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in a computer information system; or intentionally creates or spreads destructive programs such as computer viruses, thereby causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, and the consequences are serious, such conduct constitutes the crime of disrupting a computer information system.

Where a person, in violation of state regulations, uses technical means of interference to attack and hijack the public domain name servers of an Internet operator, adds instructions in the domain name servers, and implants Trojan horse viruses in a large number of personal computer information systems, thereby causing the computer information systems to be unable to operate normally, and the consequences are serious, such person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of disrupting a computer information system.

Procuratorial Authority: Binhu District People's Procuratorate of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Ma Zhisong, male, 29 years old, unemployed, residing at Shaoling Road, Wuhou District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Peng Xu, male, 31 years old, farmer, residing at Futian Village, Pengzhen, Shuangliu County, Sichuan Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Ma Zhiqiang, male, 26 years old, unemployed, residing at Dongning Town, Dongning County, Heilongjiang Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Liu Xugang, male, 23 years old, farmer, residing at Hongyuan Community, Dongning Town, Dongning County, Heilongjiang Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Tang Songjun, male, 22 years old, student, residing at No. 2 Avenue, Jianggan District, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Bu Yong (formerly known as Wei Yong), male, 26 years old, unemployed, residing at Jiefang Street, Yueyang Town, Anyue County, Ziyang City, Sichuan Province. Arrested on February 15, 2008 in connection with this case.

The Binhu District People's Procuratorate of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province filed a public prosecution with the Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province, charging the Defendants Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Tang Songjun, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, and Bu Yong with the crime of disrupting a computer information system.

The indictment alleged: From late September 2007 to mid-November 2007, the Defendants Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, Tang Songjun, and Bu Yong conspired to steal the online game account information of Internet users. Using a domain name server hijacking program, they attacked and hijacked a total of 27 domain name servers in more than 10 provinces and municipalities including Shanghai, Chongqing, and Yangzhou. As a result, when Internet users visited the homepage of Tencent's Mini Web, they were wrongly directed to a server pre-set by Ma Zhisong and others in Wuxi, which carried 17 types of online game Trojan horses, thereby becoming infected with Trojan horse viruses. Due to the attacks and hijacking by Ma Zhisong and others, Tencent was forced to temporarily close its Mini Web homepage, causing the computer information systems of Tencent's Mini Web and QQ client to be unable to operate normally, and resulting in direct economic losses of RMB 100,800 to Tencent. The conduct of Ma Zhisong and others has constituted the crime of disrupting a computer information system, and punishment was requested in accordance with the law.

On trial at first instance, the Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi City found:

The public domain name servers of Internet operators are important infrastructure of China's Internet. The function of a domain name server is to resolve a website and its corresponding IP address, enabling Internet users to access the corresponding website by entering a URL. That is, the resolution performed by a domain name server is a necessary step for an Internet user to visit a website.

In July 2007, the Defendant Ma Zhisong learned that it was possible to steal others' online game account information by hijacking domain name servers and mastered the principle of hijacking domain name servers. Subsequently, Ma Zhisong and the Defendant Peng Xu together researched and learned the specific methods of hijacking domain name servers. In August of the same year, Peng Xu, according to Ma Zhisong's requirements and ideas, wrote a domain name server hijacking program. Ma Zhisong then prepared to use the method of hijacking domain name servers to deceive Internet users, causing the domain name servers to resolve incorrectly and thereby point to his set server carrying various online game Trojan horses (a type of remote monitoring software used to collect users' online information and keyboard operations and perform remote transmission), so as to achieve the purpose of stealing users' online game account information. In September of the same year, Ma Zhisong informed the Defendants Bu Yong, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, and others of the above intention. Bu Yong contributed RMB 4,000, and Ma Zhiqiang and Liu Xugang each contributed RMB 18,000, which were used to rent the rental house, computers, servers, and other equipment for the operation. Ma Zhiqiang also rented eight servers in Wuxi Telecom Dafu IDC computer room through the Internet, which were used to store the counterfeit Tencent Mini Web homepage fabricated by Ma Zhisong and the 17 types of Trojan horses collected by Ma Zhiqiang and Liu Xugang for stealing domestic online game accounts. In early October 2007, Ma Zhisong contacted the Defendant Tang Songjun through the Internet and asked Tang Songjun to write a program for collecting addresses of domain name servers in various regions, as well as to optimize and modify downloaded Trojan horse programs, and to write a program to make the web page Trojan horses undetectable, for use in hijacking domain name servers.

From late September 2007 to mid-November 2007, Ma Zhisong and others, in Chengdu, used the compiled hijacking program to attack and hijack a total of 27 domain name servers in more than 10 provinces and municipalities including Shanghai, Chongqing, and Yangzhou. As a result, when Internet users visited the homepage of Tencent's Mini Web, they were wrongly directed to a server pre-set by Ma Zhisong and others in Wuxi, which carried 17 types of online game Trojan horses, thereby becoming infected with Trojan horse viruses. Due to the attacks and hijacking by Ma Zhisong and others, Tencent was forced to temporarily close its Mini Web homepage, causing the computer information systems of Tencent's Mini Web and QQ client to be unable to operate normally, and resulting in direct economic losses of RMB 100,800 to Tencent.

The above facts were not disputed by the Defendants Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, Tang Songjun, and Bu Yong during the trial. They are further confirmed by the following evidence: the reporting materials of Tencent; the testimony of witnesses Wang Hongpeng, Ding Xiaoliang, Jiang Yong, Wang Xiujun, Zhong Sheng, Li Jing, Chen Hui, and Zhang Jian; the Judicial Authentication Inspection Report No. Yue An Ji Si Jian (2008) No. 14 issued by Guangdong Anzheng Computer Forensic Institute; the Electronic Data Inspection and Authentication Document No. Su Gong Wang Jian Zi (2008) No. 001 issued by Jiangsu Provincial Public Security Department; the Electronic Data Inspection and Authentication Document No. Su Gong Wang Jian Zi (2008) No. 002 issued by Jiangsu Provincial Public Security Department; the Audit Report issued by Shenzhen Zhongqin Wanxin Certified Public Accountants; the Electronic Evidence Inspection Work Record prepared by the Network Police Division of Wuxi Public Security Bureau; and the Statement of Case Incident issued by Wuxi Public Security Bureau. These are sufficient to establish the facts.

The issue in dispute in this case was: whether the charges brought by the procuratorial authority against the six Defendants, Ma Zhisong and others, were established.

The Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi City held at first instance:

Pursuant to Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "the Criminal Law"), where a person, in violation of state regulations, deletes, modifies, adds, or interferes with the functions of a computer information system; or deletes, modifies, or adds the data or application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in a computer information system; or intentionally creates or spreads destructive programs such as computer viruses, thereby causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, and the consequences are serious, such conduct constitutes the crime of disrupting a computer information system. The object violated by this crime is the security of computer information systems. Article 3 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Security Protection of Computer Information Systems provides: "The security protection of computer information systems shall ensure the security of computers and their related and supporting equipment and facilities (including networks), the security of the operating environment, the security of information, and the normal functioning of computer functions, so as to maintain the secure operation of computer information systems." Where a person, in violation of state regulations, destroys the functions of a computer information system, and the consequences are serious enough to constitute a crime, punishment shall be meted out according to law. The objective aspect of this crime is that the actor has committed acts of destroying the functions of a computer information system with serious consequences. The functions of a computer information system refer to the capabilities and abilities to collect, process, store, transmit, and retrieve information according to certain application goals and rules. The specific manifestations of the conduct of this crime are: deleting, modifying, adding, or interfering with the functions of a computer information system; or deleting, modifying, or adding the data or application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in a computer information system; or intentionally creating or spreading destructive programs such as computer viruses, so that the functions of the computer information system cannot be performed normally, thereby causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally. To constitute this crime, serious consequences are also required. "Serious consequences" generally include: destruction of the functions of important national computer information systems; causing relatively large economic losses to the state, society, collectives, organizations, or individuals; causing adverse social impact; etc. The subjective aspect of this crime is intent. The actor, knowing that the illegal programs or instructions he inputs will cause the harmful result that the computer information system cannot operate normally, still desires or allows such result to occur.

The Defendants Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, Tang Songjun, and Bu Yong added instructions in the domain name servers and used the domain name server hijacking program to attack and hijack the public domain name servers of Internet operators, thereby interfering with the resolution function of the computer information systems. The hijacking and interference by Ma Zhisong and others caused Internet users visiting the homepage of Tencent's Mini Web to be wrongly directed to a server carrying Trojan horses, causing a large number of client computer information systems to be infected with Trojan horse viruses and thus unable to operate normally. To protect users' interests, Tencent was forced to temporarily close its Mini Web homepage, thereby also causing Tencent's Mini Web computer information system to be unable to operate normally, and resulting in direct economic losses of RMB 100,800 to Tencent. These consequences are serious.

In summary, the Defendants Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, Tang Songjun, and Bu Yong, in violation of state regulations, used technical means of interference to attack and hijack the public domain name servers of Internet operators, added instructions in the domain name servers, implanted Trojan horses in a large number of personal computer information systems, thereby causing the computer information systems to be unable to operate normally, with serious consequences. Their conduct has all constituted the crime of disrupting a computer information system, and it was a joint crime. According to law, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention. The facts charged by the procuratorial authority against Ma Zhisong and the other five for the crime of disrupting a computer information system are clear, the evidence is true and sufficient, and the charges are established; they are adopted. Ma Zhisong, Peng Xu, Ma Zhiqiang, Liu Xugang, and Tang Songjun played principal roles in the joint crime and are principal offenders. Bu Yong played a secondary role in the joint crime and is an accessory, and shall be given a lighter punishment. The defense opinion of Tang Songjun's defense counsel that Tang Songjun was an accessory in the joint crime is inconsistent with the facts and is not adopted. However, the defense opinion that Tang Songjun truthfully confessed his crime after being brought to justice, had a good attitude of admission, and requested a lighter punishment for Tang Songjun is adopted.

Accordingly, on September 11, 2008, the Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi City, pursuant to Article 286(1), Article 25(1), Article 26(1), and Article 27 of the Criminal Law, rendered the following judgment:

1. The Defendant Ma Zhisong is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to four years' imprisonment;

2. The Defendant Peng Xu is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to three years' imprisonment;

3. The Defendant Ma Zhiqiang is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment;

4. The Defendant Liu Xugang is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment;

5. The Defendant Tang Songjun is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to two years' imprisonment;

6. The Defendant Bu Yong is convicted of the crime of disrupting a computer information system and sentenced to one year's imprisonment.

Peng Xu and Liu Xugang both refused to accept the first-instance judgment and filed appeals with the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court. Peng Xu's grounds of appeal were: (1) He did not research the hijacking program together with the original trial defendant Ma Zhisong; (2) The conduct of attacking the domain name servers in this case did not affect Tencent. Liu Xugang's ground of appeal was: He was an accessory in the joint crime and should be given a lighter punishment. He requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment according to law.

After trial at second instance, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

The appellants Peng Xu, Liu Xugang, and the first-instance defendants Ma Zhisong, Ma Zhiqiang, Tang Songjun, and Bu Yong, in violation of state regulations, added instructions in domain name servers, implanted Trojan horses in a large number of personal computer information systems, and used technical means of interference to cause the computer information systems to be unable to operate normally, with serious consequences. Their conduct has all constituted the crime of disrupting a computer information system. In the joint crime, Peng Xu, Liu Xugang, Ma Zhisong, Ma Zhiqiang, and Tang Songjun were principal offenders, and Bu Yong was an accessory.

With respect to the grounds of appeal raised by appellant Peng Xu, the court of second instance held: (1) The fact that Peng Xu researched the public domain name server hijacking program together with the first-instance defendant Ma Zhisong was confirmed by the confessions of Peng Xu himself and Ma Zhisong, and Peng Xu also clearly acknowledged it during the first-instance trial, which is sufficient to establish the fact. (2) Although Peng Xu and others did not directly attack all of Tencent's servers, in the process of hijacking the domain name servers, they used a counterfeit Tencent Mini Web homepage carrying Trojan horse viruses, which caused the computer information systems of a large number of Tencent QQ users to be added with malicious programs. This forced Tencent to close the corresponding functions to protect the interests of QQ users, indirectly harming Tencent's interests. In summary, the grounds of appeal raised by Peng Xu cannot be established and are not adopted.

With respect to the ground of appeal raised by appellant Liu Xugang, the court of second instance held: After learning that the first-instance defendant Ma Zhisong and others could obtain computer users' online game account information by hijacking domain name servers, Liu Xugang rallied the first-instance defendant Ma Zhiqiang to go to Chengdu together, and together with Ma Zhiqiang, each contributed RMB 18,000 to purchase the equipment necessary for hijacking the public domain name servers, thereby enabling Ma Zhisong and others' series of criminal acts of attacking and hijacking domain name servers to succeed. At the same time, the Trojan horse program provided by Liu Xugang to Ma Zhisong directly intruded into a large number of personal computer information systems. Based on this, it can be determined that Liu Xugang was a principal offender in the joint crime of this case. In summary, the ground of appeal raised by Liu Xugang cannot be established and is not adopted.

In summary, the facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear, the evidence is true and sufficient, the application of law is correct, the conviction and sentencing are appropriate, and the trial procedure is lawful; the judgment should be affirmed. On October 30, 2008, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following ruling:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
